newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Foster's removes BHP and Asahi from register.
newsitem.headline: Foster's removes BHP and Asahi from register.

text.p: Foster's Brewing Group Ltd, Australia's largest and most successful brewer, said on Thursday that it would buy back 254.5 million of its shares from Japan's Asahi Breweries for A$625 million $475 million).
The company said it would pay A$2.49 per share for the Asahi stake, which represents the bulk of its 270.3 million shareholding, equivalent to about 13 percent of the fully paid shares.

Foster's also said 36.5 percent shareholder Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd would place all but 100 million of its 716.6 million Foster's shareholding to institutions and retail investors at A$2.49 per share. BHP, Australia's largest company and a blue-chip neighbour of Foster's in Melbourne, said it would offer the remaining shares to BHP shareholders.

Foster's asked the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) earlier on Thursday afternoon for a trading halt to be placed on its shares pending an announcement which would affect more than 50 percent of its issued capital.
The company said the buyback deal with Asahi was part of an arrangement in which the Japanese brewer and BHP had committed to dispose of all their Foster's shares.

Foster's president and chief executive officer Ted Kunkel said the Asahi buyback price represented a five percent discount to Foster's average price in calendar 1997. Foster's shares were three cents lower at A$2.60 ahead of the trading halt.
"Following completion of this transaction, Foster's will achieve a more diverse shareholder base," Kunkel said.
"This ends the uncertainty of the perceived market overhang of the major shareholdings."

"The buy-back will be funded from pre-existing resources and will result in an increase in gearing to 70 percent. Foster's will still retain sufficient financial resources to fund its core businesses and to pursue new investment," Kunkel said.
Foster's said BHP and Asahi directors on the brewer's board would now resign.

Foster's said the repurchase of the Asahi shares would require the approval of eligible shareholders and a buyback resolution would be put to a general meeting on July 24. BHP and Asahi cannot vote at the meeting.
The company also said an independent experts report from Grant Samuel and Associates had advised that the buyback proposal was fair and reasonable to non-associated shareholders.
Foster's has a market capitalisation of A$5.10 billion based on 1.96 billion shares outstanding.
